title: Stage outcome
description: What one stage session returns to a supervisor. Supplied by the invoker as `claude -p --json-schema "$(cat this file)"`, so no stage skill describes this shape and none should. An envelope over an ARRAY because a develop or verify gate handles several tickets in one session: singular, it reports one verdict and silently drops the rest.

stage.description: Which skill ran. Not a `next:` value — `retro` and `prototype` are stages that hold no row.

session_id.description: The UUID the supervisor pre-assigned at dispatch, echoed back. Pre-assigned rather than reported so the transcript path is a dispatch-time fact in the run log, findable when the supervisor is dead.

commits.description: Every commit SHA this session landed, in order. Empty is legitimate: a stage can correctly conclude there was nothing to write.

cost_usd.description: What this session spent. The supervisor's own spend is NOT in here — it belongs to no ticket, and a cost-per-closed-ticket figure summed from these alone omits it.

findings_parked.description: How many entries this session appended to FINDINGS.md. The only signal left that the run is learning anything, once the stage narrative is trimmed.

conventions_resolved.description: The conventions directory this session actually resolved, or null if none did. Null is a legitimate value and an escalation, never a silent pass: a stage that built against no standard is the failure `config.yml` makes conventions mandatory to prevent.

escalation.description: One sentence naming what a person must decide, or null. Null means the stage finished on its own terms; it does not mean every ticket passed.

tickets.description: One entry per ticket this session handled, in the order it handled them. Empty for a stage that holds no row.

verdict.description: The word this stage's own hand-off line prints, lowercased. Each stage reaches only its own subset; the schema carries the union because one schema serves every stage.

next.description: The stage the ticket now sits at, as written in its frontmatter. `done` is terminal and is the only value that is not a skill.

status.description: The ticket's state, as written in its frontmatter.

detail.description: A path — and where useful an anchor — to where this ticket's detail actually landed: its Notes & decisions, its QA evidence, FINDINGS.md, or the run log. FR14's guarantee that the trim moved the detail rather than deleting it is only checkable because this field exists.
